newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia raises electricity prices by 4.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia raises electricity prices by 4.9 pct.

text.p: The Slovenian government said on Thursday it would raise electricity prices by 4.9 percent next month.

"The reason is that the government wants to improve the relatively bad situation of electricity firms and to partly compensate for the damage inflicted by bad weather in December and January," Minister of Economic Activities Metod Dragonja told a news conference.
Dragonja said snow and ice had caused some two billion tolars of damage to Slovenia's electricty grid over the past two months and a half.
He added the increase was expected to raise the overall turnover of electricity producers and distributors by some 4.5 billion tolars per year from around 90 billion tolars in 1996.
Slovenia's electricity prices, which are some 40 percent below the European Union average, were raised by 2.6 percent last year.
